html:
The southern half of Korea, below the 38th parallel, under American military rule from September 1945 to August 1948. The map shows it in 1945.

The division of Korea was agreed with the Soviet Union as Japan surrendered, and Soviet forces took the north. General John R. Hodge's military government at first kept on Japanese officials and Korean police who had served Japan, which angered many Koreans. It refused to recognise the People's Republic of Korea, a network of local committees that Korean leaders had formed after liberation.

Plans for a trusteeship and a united government broke down, and the United Nations oversaw elections in the south alone in May 1948. Violence grew: the Jeju uprising, which began in April 1948, was put down with the killing of many thousands of islanders. On 15 August 1948 the Republic of Korea was proclaimed in Seoul with Syngman Rhee as president. Two years later came the Korean War. Japan was under its own American occupation at the same time.
sum: The southern half of Korea, below the 38th parallel, under American military rule from September 1945 to August 1948. The map shows it in 1945.
